Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:11:1.english: What is [the difference] between them - In what do they disagree?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:11:2.hebrew: צד אחד - כי האי גוונא: שמא יבא לידי רבית, שמא לא יבא. צד הפדייה בא לידי רבית, צד המכר אינו בא לידי רבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:11:2.english: One side [of interest] - Such as this case: perhaps it will lead to interest, [and] perhaps it will not lead [to it]. The redemption side leads to interest; the sale side does not lead to interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:11:3.hebrew: על מנת להחזיר - דרבי יהודה גופיה לא שרי אלא ע"מ להחזיר, שאם לא יהיה מכר יחזיר לו פירות שאכל, ואפילו הכי אסר ת"ק, דבשעת אכילה קאכיל רבית ועבדיה לאיסור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:11:3.english: On the condition that it be given back - For Rabbi Yehuda himself only permits [it] on the condition that it be returned, so that if it does not become a sale, he will return to him the produce that he ate; and even so, the first Tanna forbids [it], because at the time of eating he is consuming interest and has transgressed the prohibition.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:12:1.hebrew: השתא דאמר רבי ינאי - גבי פרעון הן ודמיהן שוין, דכי היכי דהן מותר, דמיהן נמי מותר, דמה לי טוב אם הם מקבל יותר ממה שדמיהן מקבל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:12:1.english: Now that Rabbi Yannai is saying - Regarding repayment, [the produce] itself and its value are equivalent, for just as [the produce] itself is permitted, its value is also permitted — for how is it better if he receives [the produce] itself than if he receives its value?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:1:1.hebrew: דמתרצנא מתניתין כוותיה - שאני רגיל לתרץ משניות שסתם רבי כברייתא שסתם הוא, ודכוותיה אמר רבא בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיא:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:1:1.english: As I resolve the Mishnah in accordance with him - For I am accustomed to resolve Mishnayot that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] taught anonymously in accordance with the baraita that he taught anonymously, and similarly Rava said in [the chapter] HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 111b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:2:1.hebrew: הגיע זמן חטין למכור - שנתייקרו, ודרך אוצרותיהן למוכרן מעתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:2:1.english: The time to sell wheat arrived - That they had risen in price, and it is the practice of those who store them to sell them from now on.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:3:1.hebrew: יש לו מותר - ולא אמרינן דלאו כאיסרו הבא לידו היכא דיש לו, דזכי בהו האי מהשתא, ואע"ג דלא משיך, כי מוקרי ברשותיה מוקרי, ולא הוי רבית, הואיל ואם בא לחזור קאי עלייהו במי שפרע. ומיהו היכא דאין לו, לאו כאיסרו הבא לידו הוא, דהיכא דיהיב ליה זוזי פוסק ואע"ג שאין לו, דיכול זה לקנותו במעות שקיבל, דחטין מצויין לו הואיל ויצא השער, אבל זה אין בידו במה יקנה, ודמי לרבית:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:3:1.english: [If] he has [it], it is permitted - And we do not say that [it is] not like his issar [coin] that came into his hand where he has [it], for this [lender] acquires them from now; and even though he has not performed meshikhah [the act of drawing], when they appreciate in value, they appreciate in his possession, and it is not interest, since if [the borrower] comes to retract, he is subject on their account to [the curse of] Mi she-para. However, where he does not have [it], it is not like his issar that came into his hand; for where one gives him zuzim [cash], he may fix a price even though [the seller] does not have [the produce], because this [seller] can buy it with the money that he received, since wheat is readily available to him once the market price has been established; but this [borrower] has nothing in his hand with which to buy, and [thus] it resembles interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:3:2.hebrew: ומאי לקח - דקתני במתני', לקח בהלואתו שהיה נושה בו דינר זהב. ולי נראה דלא גרסינן ליה, ופירוש משובש הוא שנתלה בספר. לפי שראה ברבי אושעיא נושה בחבירו מנה — דשמעינן מינה דאי הוה יהיב ליה השתא זוזי, אפילו אין לו נמי שרי — שבש מתניתין ופירשה בלוקח בהלואתו. ולא היא, לא מבעי לשבושי מתניתין בהכי. דר' אושעיא משום חטין קמאי נקיט ליה, ולמימר דיש לו מותר אע"ג דלאו כאיסרו הבא לידו, וכי אין לו אסור הואיל ולא בא איסרו לידו. אבל מתניתין, כי תנא אין לו, גבי יין תנא, שמחמת הלואה בא עליו, שהיו כבר דמי החטין מלוה עליו. אבל גבי חטין לא תנא איסורא, ואפילו אין לו שרי, דאיסרו בא לידו, ושפיר תני בה לקח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:3:2.english: And what is "acquired" - that is taught in the Mishnah? [It means] he acquired [it] for his loan, as he was owed a gold dinar by him. And to me it appears that we do not read this [in the Gemara text], and it is a mistaken explanation that was inserted into the text. Because [the glossator] saw in [the baraita of] Rabbi Oshaya "[one who] was owed a maneh by his fellow" — from which we learn that if he had given him money now, even if he did not have [the produce], it would also be permitted — he corrupted the Mishnah and explained it as [referring to] one who acquires for his loan. But this is not so; one need not corrupt the Mishnah with this. For [the baraita of] Rabbi Oshaya mentions it because of the first wheat, and to state that when he has [it], it is permitted even though it is not like his issar coming into his hand, and when he does not have [it], it is forbidden since his issar did not come into his hand. Whereas the Mishnah, when it taught "he does not have," it taught [that] regarding wine, which came upon him because of a loan, since the value of the wheat was already a loan upon him. But regarding wheat, it did not teach a prohibition, and even if he does not have [wheat] it is permitted, because his issar came into his hand, and it properly teaches regarding it "acquired."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:1.english: One may establish a loan - that he has [owed to him] by his fellow.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:2.english: Upon produce - To stipulate [repayment in] produce upon them at the current market rate [for] all the days of the year.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:3.hebrew: ולא אמרינן לא כאיסרו הבא לידו - כדתני רבי חייא דאמר לעיל, אפילו יש לו אסור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:3.english: And we do not say [it is] not like his issar that came into his hand - As Rabbi Chiyya taught, who said above [that] even if he has [produce], it is forbidden.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:4.hebrew: ושמע מינה והוא שיש לו - אבל אין לו, אין מעמידין מלוה; אבל פוסקין על ידי נתינת מעות, כדקתני מתני' (לקמן בבא מציעא דף עב:) יצא השער פוסקין, ואוקימנא מתניתין כדתני רבי אושעיא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:4.english: And conclude from it, provided that he has [produce] - But if he does not have [produce], one may not establish [repayment of] a loan [upon produce]; however, one may set a fixed price [for future delivery] by giving money [upfront], as the Mishnah teaches (later, Bava Metzia 72b): "[Once] the market price has gone out, one may set a fixed price," and we established our Mishnah in accordance with what Rabbi Oshaya taught.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:5.hebrew: ושמע מינה - מדקתני הגיע זמן חטין למכור, שם לו החטין בדמים בשער של עכשיו ביוקר, ופוסק יין כשער של עכשיו בזול — שמע מינה איתא לדרבי ינאי. דאמר: פסק על הפירות, והגיע זמנו למכור, ובא ותבעו ואין לו — מקבל הימנו הדמים כשער של עכשיו, דמה לי מקבל הן עצמן ומה לי דמיהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:4:5.english: And conclude from it - From [the fact] that [the baraita] teaches: [When] the time for wheat to be sold arrives, he assesses the wheat for him in money at the current rate, at a high price, and contracts [for] wine at the current rate, at a low price — conclude from it [that the halakha] is in accordance with [the opinion] of Rabbi Yannai, who said: [If] one contracted for produce, and its time to be sold arrived, and he came and claimed [it] from him, and he does not have [it], he accepts from him the money at the current rate; for what [difference is it] to me [if he] receives them themselves, and what [difference is it] to me [if he receives] their monetary value?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:6:1.hebrew: עושין אמנה בפירות - נותנין מעות באמנה כשער של עכשיו שיוצא בשוק, ע"מ לקבל פירות, אפילו יוקירו חטין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:6:1.english: One may make [an arrangement of] trust with regard to produce - One gives money in trust at the current rate prevailing in the market, on condition to receive produce, even if wheat rises in price.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:6:2.hebrew: ואין עושין אמנה - לפסוק על הפירות כדי לקבל דמים לכשיוקירו, דכיון דזוזי יהיב וזוזי שקיל, מחזי כרביתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:6:2.english: And one may not make [an arrangement of] trust - [That is,] to fix a price for produce in order to receive money when [the produce] increases in price, for since he gives money and takes money, it appears like interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:7:1.hebrew: אם יש לו מותר - מהא דרבי אושעיא קא מותיב. והכא דמים קא מקבל, ששם עליו דמי החטין ומקבל היין ששוה יותר ממה שנתן, ומתחילה לא קנה יין ממנו, והרי הוא כמקבל מעות דמי החטים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:7:1.english: If he has [it], it is permitted - [The Gemara] raises an objection from that [baraita] of Rabbi Oshaya. And here he is receiving monetary value, for he assessed upon him the value of the wheat and receives the wine, which is worth more than what he gave, and from the outset he did not acquire wine from him, and thus he is like one who receives money [as] the value of the wheat.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:7:2.hebrew: בשמשך - הימנו החטים מתחילה, דדמי החטין דידיה קא מקבל, דברשותיה אייקר; דמשעה שמשך, כלתה לה תורת הלואה וקיבל חובו. וכן בכולן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:7:2.english: Where he pulled - from him the wheat initially, for he is receiving the value of his own wheat, since it appreciated in his [own] possession; for from the moment he pulled [it], the status of a loan ceased and he received [payment of] his debt. And similarly with all of them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:7:3.english: That he designated a corner for him - And it teaches us that designation is a matter [of legal significance].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:8:1.english: Whose [opinion] is this - Which teaches [that if] he has [it, it is] permitted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:8:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה היא דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר - רבית שאינה על ידי הלואה אלא ע"י מכר, ופעמים שבאה על ידי רבית. כגון זו: אם יוקרו הפירות וישלם דמים, יש כאן רבית; ואם לא ישלם דמים אלא פירות שפסק הוא עמו, אין כאן רבית. היינו צד אחד ברבית — פעמים יש רבית ופעמים אין רבית, שהרי אינו פוסק עמו ע"מ לשלם דמים אלא פירות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:8:2.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda, who said [that] one-sided interest is permitted - Interest that is not by way of a loan, but rather by way of a sale, and sometimes it results in interest. Such as this [case]: if the produce increases in price and he pays money, there is interest here; and if he does not pay money, but rather [the] produce that he stipulated with him, there is no interest here. This is [what is meant by] "one-sided interest" — sometimes there is interest and sometimes there is no interest, for he does not stipulate with him on condition to pay money, but rather produce.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:9:1.hebrew: ועשה שדהו מכר - אם אין אני נותן לך מכאן עד יום פלוני, הרי השדה שלך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:9:1.english: And made his field a sale - [That is, he stipulates:] "If I do not give [it to] you from now until such-and-such a day, behold, the field is yours."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:9:2.english: When the seller consumes produce - Within the [allotted] time, [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:9:3.hebrew: לוקח אוכל פירות אסור - שמא לא יבוא לידי מכר, שיחזיר לו מעותיו, ונמצא שבהלואה היו אצלו, וזה אוכל פירות ברבית: בייתוס בן זונין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 63a:9:3.english: [If the] buyer consumes the produce, [it is] prohibited - Lest it not result in a sale, as [the seller] will return his money to him, and it will turn out that [the money] was with him as a loan, and this [lender] is consuming produce as interest. Baitos ben Zunin:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:11:1.hebrew: רבית על מנת להחזיר איכא בינייהו - ואם תאמר: מאי טעמא דרבנן דאסרי, דאיזה רבית הוא זה? והלא כשיבא לפדות מנכה לו תחילה פירות שאכל? וי"ל: ודאי אם הוא עושה כן לא הוי רבית, אלא מצריכו לפרוע תחילה הכל קודם שינכה לו כלום, ואם לא יוכל לפרוע לו הכל, תהא משוקעת בידו. ואם תאמר: דתנן בערכין (דף לא ושם ד"ה והתניא): "המוכר בית בבתי ערי חומה גואל מיד וגואל עד שנים עשר חדש, הרי זו כמו רבית ואינו רבית", ופריך בגמ': "והתניא רבית גמורה היא? אלא התורה התירה!" ומשני: "הא ר' יהודה והא רבנן." והשתא לרבא, דלכולי עלמא צד אחד ברבית אסור, היכי משני? ויש לומר: דמדאורייתא מודה רבא דבצד אחד ברבית פליגי, אבל מדרבנן נראה לרבא דליכא למאן דשרי; ורבי יהודה שרי הכא אפילו מדרבנן, כדמוכח בעובדא דמייתי, לכך מוקי רבא דאיירי ברבית על מנת להחזיר. ואם תאמר: בפרק בתרא דמגילה (דף כז: ושם ד"ה רבי) תנא: "אין מוכרין בית הכנסת אלא על תנאי אימתי שירצה שיחזור, דברי רבי מאיר", ופריך בגמרא: "ולרבי מאיר היכי דיירי ביה? הא הוה ליה רבית!" ומשני: "סבר לה כרבי יהודה דאמר צד אחד ברבית מותר". וי"ל: לרבא איירי התם כגון שהתנו עמו שאם יפדו יתן השכר על שדר בו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:11:1.english: The [difference] between them is interest [taken] on condition to return [it] - And if you ask: What is the reason of the Rabbis who prohibit [it], for what [kind of] interest is this? Does [the buyer] not first deduct for him the produce that he ate when he comes to redeem [it]? And one can say: Certainly if he does so, it is not interest; rather, he requires him to pay everything first before he deducts anything for him, and if he is unable to pay him everything, [the field] remains permanently in his possession. And if you ask: We learned in a Mishnah in Arakhin (31a, and there s.v. Vehatanya): "One who sells a house among the houses of walled cities may redeem [it] immediately and may redeem [it] up to twelve months; this is like interest, yet it is not interest." And the Gemara asks: "Was it not taught in a baraita that it is full-fledged interest, except that the Torah permitted it?" And [the Gemara] answers: "This [Mishnah] is Rabbi Yehuda, and that [baraita] is the Rabbis." Now, according to Rava, [who holds] that according to everyone, one-sided interest is prohibited, how does [the Gemara] answer? And one can say: On a Torah level, Rava agrees that they disagree about one-sided interest, but on a rabbinic level, it appears to Rava that there is no one who permits [it]; whereas Rabbi Yehuda permits [it] here even on a rabbinic level, as is proven from the incident that [the Gemara] cites. Therefore, Rava establishes that [here] it is dealing with interest [taken] on condition to return [it]. And if you ask: In the last chapter of Megillah (27b, and there s.v. Rabbi), it was taught: "One may only sell a synagogue on condition [that] whenever [the town] wishes, it may revert [to them] — [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir." And the Gemara asks: "And according to Rabbi Meir, how may [the buyers] dwell in it? Surely that is interest!" And [the Gemara] answers: "He holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who says one-sided interest is permitted." And one can say: According to Rava, there it is dealing with a case where they stipulated with him that if they redeem [it], he will pay rent for [the time] he dwelled in it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:5:1.hebrew: דאמר רבי ינאי מה לי הן - החטין, מה לי דמיהן — כגון יין, אם יש לו; כך פי' רבינו שמואל, ור"ל: דוקא יין, אבל מעות אסור. ואין נראה לר"ת, דבפרק הגוזל [קמא] (ב"ק דף קג. ושם ד"ה התם), גבי רב כהנא זבין כתנא ואייקר זבנוה מרוותא קמאי, א"ל לרב: אשקול זוזי? אמר ליה: אי כי מזבני אמרי כתנא דכהנא הוא — שרי, ואם לאו — אסור; רב לטעמיה דאמר אין עושין אמנה בדמים — משמע דלר' ינאי שרי למשקל זוזי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:5:1.english: As Rabbi Yannai says: What [difference is it] to me [if] they - [i.e.,] the wheat, [or] "what [difference is it] to me [if he takes] their value" — such as wine, if he has [wine]; so explained Rabbeinu Shmuel, and he means to say: specifically wine, whereas money is forbidden. But this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for in the chapter HaGozel [Kamma] (Bava Kamma 103a, and there s.v. hatam), regarding [the case where] Rav Kahana bought flax and it appreciated [and] the original owners sold it, [Rav Kahana] said to Rav: "May I take the money?" [Rav] said to him: "If when they sold it they said, 'It is Kahana's flax,' it is permitted, and if not, it is forbidden" — [which is] Rav following his own view, as he says one may not make a trust arrangement [amanah] for money; this implies that according to Rabbi Yannai, it is permitted to take money.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:7:1.hebrew: בשמשך - ואפילו אכלן המוכר, מותר לשלם חטים אחרים אם יוקירו, ולא דמי לסאה בסאה דאסור (לעיל בבא מציעא דף סב.), משום דהתם הלואה והכא זביני. ומשיכה דהכא לא הויא אלא לענין היתר פיסוק, ולא לקנות ממש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:7:1.english: Where [the buyer] pulled [the produce] - And even if the seller ate them, it is permitted [for him] to pay [with] other wheat if it appreciates [in price], and it is not comparable to [a loan of] a se'ah for a se'ah, which is forbidden (above, Bava Metzia 62a), because there it is a loan, whereas here it is a sale. And the pulling [mentioned] here is only with respect to permitting fixing a price [in advance], and not to acquire [the produce] outright.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:8:1.hebrew: צד אחד ברבית מותר - ואע"ג דבשעת הפרעון הוי רבית, כיון שבשעת הפסק הוי צד אחד של היתר — שרי. וא"ת: א"כ, סאה בסאה נמי יהא מותר ללות לרבי יהודה, דצד אחד הוא, דשמא לא יוקירו — דבהלואה נמי שרי רבי יהודה צד אחד ברבית, כדאמרינן לקמן (בבא מציעא דף סה:) גבי "משכן לו בית, משכן לו שדה": "הא דלא כר' יהודה"? ויש לומר: דלא חשיב צד אחד ברבית אלא דבר שיש ביד מלוה או ביד לוה לעשות צד אחד שלא יהא רבית; ולא דמי לסאה בסאה, שתלוי בשער וע"כ יהא רבית אם יוקירו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 63a:8:1.english: One-sided interest is permitted - Even though at the time of payment it is interest, since at the time of the agreement there is one side of permissibility, it is permitted. And if you ask: If so, [borrowing] a se'ah for a se'ah should also be permitted to borrow according to Rabbi Yehuda, since it is one-sided, as perhaps [the prices] will not rise — for even in a loan Rabbi Yehuda permits one-sided interest, as we say later (Bava Metzia 65b) regarding "If one mortgaged a house to him [or] mortgaged a field to him": "This is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda"? And one can answer: It is not considered one-sided interest unless it is something where it is in the power of the lender or in the power of the borrower to bring about the one side where there will not be interest; and it is not similar to [borrowing] a se'ah for a se'ah, which depends on the market price, and it will perforce be interest if [prices] rise.
